_what: APPEND-ONLY CONTENT DELTA for schema/class-frame-v1.json — electrical. Not a replacement file.
_why: Two authors: Builder Code owns the structure, the design session owns the five content arrays. Whole-file sends revert structural work.
_cutFrom: the 68-class state as merged in PR #61, read from the source rather than from a working copy — the failure the last delta's _replaceWholesale carried.
_howToApply: Append each array below to the array of the same name. No existing entry modified, no id collision — verified against the 68-class state.
_noStatusBlock: Deliberately absent. `status` and `contentPassProgress.written` are derived from `classes` and tested since PR #61, so a restatement here would be the stale claim that guard was built to catch. `contentPassProgress.remaining` is prose and is the one thing that needs a human edit: drop `electrical`.

_ownerRulingsThisSystemRestsOn.electrical: Anything touching electrical for compensation must be done by a licensed electrician. Doorbells, thermostats, smart-home devices and seasonal lighting are not.
_ownerRulingsThisSystemRestsOn.consequence: `electrical-panel` declares ZERO care categories and that is the ruling, not an omission — every act that would maintain a panel is licensed work. `no-gfci-in-wet-location` reads as coordination. The exception is the generator: an engine is not a circuit, so running and servicing one is ours.
_ownerRulingsThisSystemRestsOn.theLineItDraws: Operating a device to learn is inspection; altering a circuit is licensed work. That is why `gfci-test-function` is an inspection point rather than a care category — pressing test and reset changes nothing.
_ownerRulingsThisSystemRestsOn.notEncodedHere: Per Amendment 6 and the water-heating pilot §1a, the class list assigns no labour. These rulings shaped what the content SAYS; no licensing field was added, and none should be.

careCategories.label: Generator exercise run
careCategories.note: The one care item in this system that is not licensed work — running a machine, not altering a circuit.

careCategories.label: Engine oil and filter service
careCategories.note: Standby and portable generators. Consumable — §1b part identity.

careCategories.label: Battery replacement
careCategories.note: Consumable — §1b. Shared with safety devices and controls.

careCategories.label: Stored fuel rotation
careCategories.note: Portable generators only. Fuel that sat two winters is why the generator does not start in the outage it was bought for.

careCategories.label: Panel surface cleaning
careCategories.note: Solar. Height work, which the owner ruled is HouseSteady labour.

careCategories.label: Connector cleaning
careCategories.note: EV charging handles and their contacts.

inspectionPoints.label: Enclosure exterior condition
inspectionPoints.note: Visual only, from outside the enclosure — the schedule's own caution. Everything inside a panel is an electrician's, so this point is the whole of what we can honestly say.

inspectionPoints.label: Circuit labelling legibility
inspectionPoints.note: A legible directory is the single most useful thing in a panel to a household in an emergency, and it needs nothing opened.

inspectionPoints.label: Working clearance in front of the panel
Panel interior condition
inspectionPoints.note: Behind the dead front. Never ours — the schedule's caution says visual only from outside. Seen when an electrician is already there.

inspectionPoints.label: GFCI test and reset function
inspectionPoints.note: Pressing a test button is operating a device to learn, not altering a circuit — the line the owner drew. Direct.

inspectionPoints.label: Service mast and drop condition
inspectionPoints.note: Exposed to trees, ice and storms on rural lots while the interior panel is untouched.

inspectionPoints.label: Surge protector status indicator
inspectionPoints.note: Sacrificial by design. It reports its own death on a small light nobody looks at.

inspectionPoints.label: Transfer switch or interlock present
inspectionPoints.note: A portable generator back-feeding through a cord and no interlock is the failure this exists to find.

inspectionPoints.label: Array mounting and roof flashing
inspectionPoints.note: The roof penetration is the part that leaks, and it is nobody's job by default — not the roofer's after installation and not the solar company's after warranty.

inspectionPoints.label: Charger mounting and cable strain relief

opportunityConditions.label: Panel with no legible circuit directory
opportunityConditions.note: Cheap, coordinated, and the household feels it the first time a breaker trips at night.

opportunityConditions.label: Surge protector already spent
opportunityConditions.note: It is still installed, still looks right, and has been protecting nothing since the storm that killed it.

opportunityConditions.label: Generator with no transfer switch or interlock
Wet location with no GFCI protection
opportunityConditions.note: Coordinated work — an electrician's, per the owner's ruling on electrical for compensation.

opportunityConditions.label: Well or septic with no backup power
opportunityConditions.note: Regional. A power cut on a well-and-septic property takes water and wastewater with it, and that is a habitability question rather than a comfort one.

ownerQuestions.label: Has anything tripped or lost power repeatedly?
ownerQuestions.note: Households know exactly which breaker misbehaves and it appears in no record.

ownerQuestions.label: When was the generator last run under load?
Who installed it, and is it still under warranty?
ownerQuestions.note: Solar and EV equipment are young enough that warranty is usually live and usually unfiled.

classes.label: Electrical panel
classes.note: Zero care categories, and that is the ruling rather than an omission: every act that would maintain a panel is licensed electrical work. Three of its four inspection points are the whole of what can be honestly said from outside the enclosure, and the fourth is access-gated on an electrician already being there.

classes.label: Whole-home surge protector
classes.note: Sacrificial by design and it reports its own death on a small light nobody looks at. One inspection point, high value, and it is exactly the kind of thing a documented house catches and an undocumented one does not.

classes.label: Service mast and meter base
classes.note: Exposed to trees, ice and storms on rural lots while the interior panel is untouched. Regional.

classes.label: GFCI outlet
classes.note: Its one care-adjacent act — pressing test and reset — is inspection under the owner's line: operating a device to learn is not altering a circuit.

classes.label: Standby generator
classes.note: The exception in this system: a generator is an engine, and running and servicing an engine is not electrical work. Three care categories where the panel has none.

classes.label: Portable generator
classes.note: Splits from standby on stored fuel and on the interlock question. Fuel that sat two winters is why it does not start in the outage it was bought for.

classes.label: Generator inlet and interlock
classes.note: A portable generator often connects through one of these rather than a transfer switch, and a cord back-feeding a dryer outlet with no interlock is the failure this class exists to name.

classes.label: Solar panels
classes.note: The panels are not the inverter and outlive it by decades. Its highest-value inspection point is the roof penetration, which is nobody's job by default.

classes.label: Solar inverter
classes.note: Shortest lifespan in a solar system by a wide margin, which is the entire reason it is not merged with the array.

classes.label: EV charger
classes.note: Stub component type at config v1.11.0 — reported, not an error. Fourth stub mapping in the frame.
